en-US.author: DarthDemono
en-US.description: Network reachability and diagnostics tool with TCP, UDP, ICMP and HTTP(S) checks, traceroute, latency statistics and a health verdict.
en-US.longDescription:
PingDD is a cross-platform network reachability and diagnostics tool written in C. Where classic ping only answers whether a host replies over ICMP, PingDD checks whether the service port is actually open over TCP, UDP or ICMP, measures connection latency to microsecond precision, and falls through IPv4 and IPv6 addresses automatically. It began as a TCP ping, which is where the name comes from.

Checks: TCP and UDP port checks, ICMP echo, an HTTP and HTTPS probe (status code, connect and total latency, and the negotiated TLS version and cipher, with a bundled TLS stack), and a hop-by-hop traceroute. Addresses can be annotated with reverse DNS and origin ASN.

Analysis: many hosts, ports (lists and ranges) and protocols probed at once, sequentially or concurrently; summary statistics (min, max, average, standard deviation, p50, p95 and p99); and live network-quality diagnostics (downtime, packet loss, jitter, latency spikes, a bufferbloat estimate and DNS timing) reduced to a one-word verdict of HEALTHY, DEGRADED or DOWN. Operator modes cover continuous availability monitoring, load testing and a resilience sweep.

Output: colored text, JSON, CSV, or a Prometheus and OpenMetrics report for dashboards. Persistent options can be kept in a small config file.
en-US.name: PingDD
